While the story features complex, flawed characters—such as the narrator (who avoids visiting their hospitalized mother, driving down and turning back twice, and leaves dirty dishes for their frail mother at the end), the mother (who is stoic, stubborn, and critical), and the brother Gerry (who is neglectful and absent)—the narrative is told strictly from a single first-person perspective. It does not dive into the mindsets of diverse perspectives or present the viewpoints of other characters like Gerry. Furthermore, while the narrator's own morally ambiguous actions are acknowledged ("which I do not say in my defense"), the story relies on unspoken subtext and emotional avoidance rather than deeply exploring the motivations and beliefs behind these objectionable behaviors.
